description: **Preempt a conversation's write lock.** DSH's write lock is a cross-process kernel semaphore that never expires while its holder lives, and no API can take it away: the only means is killing the holder, so this tool first works out who that is. (1) If the lock is actually free, a normal resume follows and nothing is killed. (2) If the holder is **an orphan this server left behind** (the MCP crashed or restarted while the child lived on holding the lock), it is **killed and taken over automatically**; this is safe. (3) If the holder is **another live dsh-any-agent instance**, the request is refused unless force=true. (4) If the holder cannot be identified (**most likely your own DSH GUI has this conversation open**) it is **never killed** (that would take your UI and the conversation you are reading down with it): it is only reported, so you can close the conversation in that window and retry. Killing a holder that is running a turn interrupts that turn (logged as interrupted); the conversation itself is unharmed.

conversation_id.description: Conversation id, from dsh_start or dsh_list.

force.description: Only for the "another live dsh-any-agent instance holds it" case; it has no effect on a GUI or unknown holder (never killed).

name: dsh_takeover
title: Take over write lock
